Authoring.population_scale_cpu.note: spawn 1 body/step into an accumulating scene; fits cost(k)=a+b*k, prints drift vs 0.50 budget (NVBugs 6664721)

tests/benchmarks/benchmarks/AuthoringPop.description: Diagnostic (hidden). Incremental spawn SCALING for NVBugs 6664721: one body is authored, sealed, drained and stepped per measured step into an ACCUMULATING attached scene (never reset), so step k is the cost of adding the (k+1)-th body to a scene already holding k. The same single-body author/drain sequence as `Authoring.population_add_drip_cpu` (AuthoringCommon.h), which reloads a fresh scene per step and therefore cannot see growth. endRun() fits cost(k)=a+b*k over 150 spawns (first 3 excluded as warm-up) and prints the ticket's drift metric slope*n/median(Q1) against the 0.50 budget plus quartile medians, so trunk-vs-optimized scaling is directly comparable.

requires --forceGpu; conventional GPU dynamics, DirectGPU refused

tests/benchmarks/benchmarks/ContactRepor.description: One 1/60-second step plus the public raw contact-report pull for 512 persistent isolated reporter/static pairs. A contact is one place where two collision shapes touch; after each physics step the contact report is the list of touching pairs plus the point, normal, separation, and impulse data generated for those touches. The fixture intentionally expects no friction anchors. The `_gpu` row requires conventional GPU dynamics (`--forceGpu`) and explicitly rejects `--directGpu`, which disables the host simulation-state readback path the public raw getter reads from -- the row fails instead of publishing a misleading zero or fallback measurement. Both rows are hidden and run in separate fresh processes.

tests/benchmarks/benchmarks/OutputRead.c.description: Physics-output read vs. tensor-binding read across N bodies/links/DOFs/articulations (cubes20 or cartpole cloned to N envs, or an authored asset for vehicle/particle/deformable families). `queryread_rb` opens, drains, and releases a query every call; `readonly_*` holds the query open across steps, isolating per-frame query cost against `queryread_rb`; `tensorbinding_*` reads the same payload through a persistent tensor binding; `tensorcreate_rb` measures the tensor-binding create+spec+destroy setup the binding amortises. `_gpu` rows require DirectGPU (`--forceGpu --directGpu`) and are hidden. **Residency note:** the output read (`ovphysx_read()` / `ovphysx_fetch_read_next()`) is host-backed even on a DirectGPU scene -- only the tensor-binding destination moves to device memory there (`kDLCUDA`, ADR-0008). The `readonly_*`/`queryread_rb`/`tensorcreate_rb` GPU rows and their `tensorbinding_*` counterparts are therefore NOT like-for-like on residency; read each row's own CPU/GPU delta rather than comparing read vs. binding as a residency ratio.

tests/benchmarks/benchmarks/WriteScaling.description: `velocity_ovstage_4096_cpu` is the **primary KPI**: a 4,096-body linear-velocity write through OVStage, write completion, query release, velocity-scoped floor, update, and a 1/60s step. `velocity_tensor_4096_cpu` is the comparator: the same step shape but writing a persistent [4096,6] tensor instead. The two use different wait/seal boundaries than the Authoring.* rows above (single-seal-wait vs. separate waits) -- not directly comparable across files; see README's Comparability boundary section. The four hidden `WriteScalingHighN.*` rows are the same fixture at 8,192 and 16,384 bodies with nothing else changed; they carry a separate family prefix so the frozen L1B `WriteScaling.*` selection still returns exactly the two 4,096-body rows, and they are non-paging diagnostics (REQ-CAPI-BENCHMARK-005).
